name: offline_protocol_v1_1
extends: configs/offline_protocol_v1.json (unchanged; v1 analyses run exactly as declared there)
status: declared after training/freezing the v7 models and before any test-split metric was computed; based only on client counts per crawler family, not on model outputs
motivation: The v1 split groups by client (anonymised IP). EClog bots are self-declared crawlers that use many IPs: of the 942 scored bot clients, 505 are bingbot and 287 mj12bot, present in every split. Client-grouped test metrics therefore measure generalisation to new IPs of known crawlers, not to unseen bots.

family_tagging.rule: family of a client = most frequent label_eclog.py bot pattern among its bot-labelled requests (generic patterns resolved to the UA product token); 29 of 942 scored bot clients have purity < 0.9 and are assigned to their majority family (reported)

leave_one_family_out.train: prefix rows of train-split sessions, minus all sessions of the held-out fold's bot clients; human sessions unchanged
leave_one_family_out.model: same features and estimator settings as eclog6m_prefix_8feature_v1 (no tuning)
leave_one_family_out.threshold: smallest threshold with validation client-level FPR <= 1 % (validation humans only), as in v1
metrics: recall of the held-out fold's scored bot clients from ALL splits (none were trained on), Clopper-Pearson 95 %
ROC-AUC of held-out fold bot clients vs test-split human clients, client-cluster bootstrap 95 % (2000, seed 42)
test-split human client FPR at the threshold, Clopper-Pearson 95 %
reference: eclog6m_prefix_8feature_v1 (fold seen in training) recall on the fold's test-split bot clients
reference: frozen eclog_timing_binary_model at 0.35 on the fold's validation+test bot clients (train-split clients excluded: may overlap its one-day training clients)

v1_test_reporting_addendum: v1 test-split recall is also broken down by crawler fold
